name: Paris
fun_fact: The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer, because its iron expands in the heat.

geography: About 2.1 million people live in the city itself.
A river splits the city into a north bank and a south bank.
food: Croissants for breakfast, steak frites for dinner.
famous_for: A wrought-iron tower built for the 1889 World's Fair.

name: Wrocław
fun_fact: The bronze dwarfs started as a symbol of the Orange Alternative, an anti-communist protest movement of the 1980s.

geography: The city is spread over a dozen islands linked by more than 100 bridges.
food: Pierogi and żurek, a sour rye soup.
famous_for: Hundreds of small bronze dwarf statues hide in its streets.

name: Tokyo
fun_fact: The city was called Edo until 1868.

geography: Its metropolitan area is the most populous in the world, with about 37 million people.
It sits on a large bay on the Pacific coast.
famous_for: One of the busiest pedestrian crossings in the world, at Shibuya.

name: Lisbon
fun_fact: A huge earthquake in 1755 destroyed most of the city.

geography: It is built on seven hills above a wide river estuary.
It is the westernmost capital of mainland Europe.
food: Pastel de nata, a custard tart, and grilled sardines.
famous_for: Old yellow trams climbing its steep streets, like the famous tram 28.

name: Buenos Aires
fun_fact: Avenida 9 de Julio is one of the widest avenues in the world.

geography: It lies on the Río de la Plata, one of the widest river estuaries in the world.
About 15 million people live in its metropolitan area.
language: People say "Hola" and use "vos" instead of "tú".
food: Asado, empanadas and dulce de leche.
famous_for: Tango was born in its port neighbourhoods.
